cards.front: Recall a key point about Educational Achievement & Inequality
cards.back: Social class and achievement: working-class students consistently achieve less well than middle-class students. External factors: material deprivation (poorer housing, less study space, no internet), cultural deprivation (Bernstein: restricted code vs elaborated code), cultural capital (Bourdieu: middle-class knowledge, tastes and values give advantage in school). Internal factors: streaming and labelling (Becker: teachers have an 'ideal pupil' image that is middle-class).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Educational Achievement & Inequality
cards.back: Gender and achievement: girls now outperform boys at every level (61% of girls vs 50% of boys achieve 5+ GCSEs A*-C). Reasons for girls' improvement: feminism (changed aspirations), changing family patterns (more women-headed households), employment opportunities (more jobs for women), GCSE coursework favoured girls. Reasons for boys' underachievement: laddish subcultures (Epstein: working-class boys see academic work as 'unmasculine'), male role model deficit (few male primary teachers).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Educational Achievement & Inequality
cards.back: Ethnicity and achievement: Chinese and Indian students achieve above the national average; Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Black Caribbean students achieve below. External factors: language barriers (English as additional language), material deprivation (higher poverty rates among some ethnic groups), family structure (more lone-parent families among Black Caribbean). Internal factors: teacher labelling (Gillborn and Youdell: teachers have lower expectations of Black students), institutional racism (policies that inadvertently disadvantage ethnic minorities), ethnocentric curriculum.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Educational Achievement & Inequality
cards.back: Labelling and self-fulfilling prophecy: Rosenthal and Jacobson's Pygmalion study showed that teacher expectations influenced student performance. Students labelled as 'bright' improved; those labelled as 'slow' declined. Becker: teachers judge students against the 'ideal pupil' (middle-class, compliant, motivated).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Educational Achievement & Inequality
cards.back: Streaming and setting: students are placed in ability groups. Hargreaves: streaming creates anti-school subcultures in lower streams (students reject school values because the school has rejected them). Gillborn and Youdell: the 'educational triage' - schools categorise students as those who will pass anyway, those with potential to improve, and hopeless cases - working-class and Black students are disproportionately placed in the 'hopeless' category.

cards.front: What should you know about sociology exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing educational inequality, always: distinguish external from internal factors, use named studies (Bourdieu, Bernstein, Becker, Gillborn), and evaluate which factors are most important for each group (class, gender, ethnicity).

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Differences in educational achievement are due to natural differences in intelligence between social groups.
